questions.q: Why does this course close on a communication lesson rather than a sixth technical domain?
options: Because communication is unrelated to architecture work
Because there are only five domains and a sixth would be redundant by coincidence
Because executives never need to understand technical decisions
Because none of the course's technical breadth does any good if it can't actually reach the people who need to fund, approve, build, or defend it
questions.explain: Communication is described as the connective tissue that makes everything else in the course actually land in the real world — breadth and process mean little if they can't reach and persuade the people who act on them.

questions.q: What three things does a strong executive brief on a technical decision cover, per this lesson?
options: What's being proposed, what it costs to say yes, and what it costs to say no
The full data model, the integration pattern, and the sharing rules involved
The names of every stakeholder consulted during the project
A complete technical walkthrough of every alternative considered
questions.explain: A strong executive brief fits in roughly three sentences: what's proposed, the cost of saying yes (time, money, risk accepted), and the cost of saying no (risk or opportunity cost of not proceeding) — not the technical journey that produced the recommendation.

questions.q: Where should the detailed technical reasoning behind an executive-facing recommendation actually live?
options: Nowhere; it should never be written down
Only in the architect's personal notes, inaccessible to anyone else
Documented in the blueprint from Lesson 10, available if asked for, but not in the first thirty seconds of an executive's attention
It should always be the first thing presented to an executive
questions.explain: The underlying data model, integration pattern, and risk analysis should exist and be documented (per Lesson 10's blueprint), but an executive brief leads with the decision and its cost, not the technical path that produced it.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect its communication skills to the CTA Architect Review Board format described in Lesson 1?
options: It claims this course is itself full CTA exam preparation

It explains that the review board's presentation-and-defense format directly draws on this course's decision structure, risk framing, and audience-reading skills, even though scenario-drilling exam prep comes later in the path
It says the review board has no connection to communication skills at all
It claims the review board only tests pure technical trivia with no presentation component
questions.explain: The review board's challenge-and-defend format relies directly on skills this course built — decision structure, constraints/assumptions discipline, risk framing, and audience-reading — even though this course isn't itself CTA exam prep.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what comes next in the Technical Architect path after this course?
options: Nothing; this is the final course in the entire Salesforce Architect destination
A direct jump straight to sitting the CTA Architect Review Board exam with no further coursework
A repeat of this same course at a more advanced reading level

Dedicated, course-length treatment of each domain this course introduced: data architecture, integration architecture, identity and access management, security architecture, and development lifecycle and deployment
questions.explain: This course is described as the entry point whose breadth sets up deeper, dedicated courses on each domain later in the path, building toward eventual review-board preparation.
